featured_projects.title: AI Threat Detection Engine
featured_projects.description: AI-powered threat detection engine that analyzes nginx access logs using a 3-model ML ensemble (Autoencoder, Random Forest, Isolation Forest) exported to ONNX to classify HTTP traffic as benign or malicious in real-time with sub-millisecond inference.
features: 3-model ML ensemble (Autoencoder + Random Forest + Isolation Forest) exported to ONNX for sub-millisecond CPU inference
4-stage async pipeline: parses raw access logs, extracts 35-dimensional feature vectors, scores via rules + ML, dispatches alerts
Rule engine with ModSecurity CRS-inspired detection patterns for SQLi, XSS, path traversal, command injection, Log4Shell, and SSRF
Real-time WebSocket alert feed streaming live severity scoring, threat classification, and confidence metrics to a React dashboard
Deploys as a lightweight Docker sidecar alongside any nginx-based web infrastructure with zero code modification

case_study.problem: Traditional web application firewalls rely solely on static regex signatures that struggle with zero-day evasion, while heavy ML pipelines introduce unacceptable request latency.
case_study.built: Architected an asynchronous 4-stage pipeline that pairs instant rule matching with a 3-model ML ensemble exported to ONNX for sub-millisecond CPU scoring.
decisions: Used ONNX runtime for CPU inference to avoid GPU dependency in container sidecars
Combined unsupervised anomaly detection (Autoencoder + Isolation Forest) with supervised classification (Random Forest)
Streamed detection events over WebSockets to decouple inference from dashboard rendering
Packaged as a drop-in Docker sidecar that mounts nginx log volumes directly
case_study.outcome: Achieved real-time classification of HTTP attacks (SQLi, XSS, SSRF) with sub-millisecond inference latency and zero downtime.

featured_projects.title: SOC Automation Lab (Wazuh, Shuffle, TheHive)
featured_projects.description: End-to-end Security Operations Center (SOC) automation lab integrating Wazuh SIEM for host and network detection, Shuffle SOAR for automated response workflows, and TheHive for centralized incident case management.
features: Wazuh SIEM monitoring Windows endpoints and Linux servers with custom rules detecting Mimikatz credential dumping and lateral movement
Shuffle SOAR workflow engine receiving webhook alerts, parsing IoCs, and querying VirusTotal and AbuseIPDB for automated enrichment
TheHive incident response platform automatically generating alert cases with enriched observables, severity ratings, and task checklists
Automated threat containment action triggers that isolate compromised endpoints and block malicious IPs at the perimeter
Complete telemetry pipeline using Sysmon on endpoints for granular process creation, network connection, and LSASS access tracking

case_study.problem: Security analysts in enterprise SOCs face overwhelming alert fatigue and slow manual triage when correlating endpoint telemetry with threat intelligence.
case_study.built: Constructed an automated detection and response ecosystem connecting Wazuh SIEM, Shuffle SOAR webhooks, and TheHive case management.
decisions: Deployed Sysmon with customized configuration to catch credential theft techniques (LSASS access, Mimikatz)
Automated tier-1 triage by orchestrating VirusTotal and AbuseIPDB API lookups inside Shuffle SOAR
Configured webhooks to automatically escalate High and Critical alerts directly to TheHive with actionable forensic tasks
case_study.outcome: Reduced incident triage and enrichment time from 15+ minutes per alert down to under 5 seconds with full contextual observables.

featured_projects.title: Security Incident Response Automation on AWS
featured_projects.description: Production-ready incident response automation architecture that ingests security findings from AWS Security Hub and Amazon GuardDuty via EventBridge, triggering automated Lambda containment playbooks and SNS notifications.
features: Event-driven architecture using Amazon EventBridge rules to filter findings from AWS Security Hub and Amazon GuardDuty in real-time
Automated containment playbooks executed by AWS Lambda: isolates compromised EC2 instances, revokes compromised IAM sessions, and applies deny-all NACLs
Multi-channel alerting via Amazon SNS delivering structured JSON summaries and actionable remediation links to security engineering teams
Comprehensive audit logging: every triggered action, finding snapshot, and containment status recorded in CloudWatch and DynamoDB
Least-privilege IAM execution roles with granular resource-based policies ensuring remediation Lambdas only modify affected target resources

case_study.problem: Cloud environments experience credential exfiltration and unauthorized resource access that require immediate containment before human operators can respond.
case_study.built: Developed a serverless automated incident response framework deploying EventBridge-triggered Lambda containment playbooks across Security Hub findings.
decisions: Used EventBridge pattern filtering to trigger containment only on High and Critical findings
Created deterministic isolation actions (security group swapping, IAM session invalidation) that preserve forensic state
Employed SNS topics with dead-letter queues to guarantee alert delivery without dropping notifications
case_study.outcome: Contained compromised cloud instances and invalidated leaked IAM credentials within 3 seconds of GuardDuty detection.

featured_projects.title: Advanced Blue-Green Deployments with CodeDeploy
featured_projects.description: Sophisticated zero-downtime deployment pipeline for containerized microservices on Amazon ECS and serverless AWS Lambda, featuring traffic shifting via Application Load Balancer and automated CloudWatch alarm-driven rollbacks.
features: Zero-downtime blue/green deployment strategy routing live production traffic across twin target groups on Application Load Balancer
Automated canary and linear traffic shifting schedules (e.g. Canary 10% 5min, then 90%) validating service health before full cutover
CloudWatch 5xx error rate and p99 latency alarms configured as automated rollback triggers in CodeDeploy for instant failsafe recovery
Pre-traffic and post-traffic lifecycle validation hooks powered by Lambda functions running smoke tests against the green target group
Reusable infrastructure-as-code modules managing ECS task definitions, service configurations, and CodeDeploy deployment groups

case_study.problem: Traditional rolling deployments risk service interruption, expose all users to bugs simultaneously, and require slow manual rollback procedures.
case_study.built: Engineered an automated blue/green pipeline pairing ALB traffic shifting with CodeDeploy lifecycle hooks and CloudWatch alarm rollbacks.
decisions: Utilized dual ALB target groups so green environments can be fully validated before receiving production traffic
Configured automated rollback triggers on p99 latency spikes and HTTP 5xx error thresholds
Implemented pre-traffic Lambda hook to run database schema compatibility checks prior to switching listeners
case_study.outcome: Achieved 100% zero-downtime deployments with automated rollback within 60 seconds if error thresholds are breached.

featured_projects.title: TOR-UNVEIL: Network Forensics & Deanonymization
featured_projects.description: Cybersecurity research and forensics platform developed to trace Tor network traffic by correlating statistical activity patterns, consensus relay descriptors, entry guard node timing, and PCAP packet captures with confidence scoring.
features: Automated harvesting and parsing of Tor consensus data, bandwidth authorities, and relay descriptor metrics
Statistical flow correlation matching packet timing and byte-size bursts between capture points and relay activity windows
Entry guard node identification algorithm narrowing origin networks through intersection and uptime probability scoring
Interactive network topology visualization plotting relay circuits, confidence intervals, and timeline reconstructions
PCAP parser analyzing encrypted packet streams, inter-packet arrival times, and TLS handshake fingerprints

case_study.problem: Anonymity networks like Tor conceal threat actor command-and-control infrastructure, creating significant challenges for digital forensics and incident investigations.
case_study.built: Created an analytical forensic framework that ingests network packet captures and correlates traffic bursts against Tor consensus relay telemetry.
decisions: Applied statistical timing-correlation algorithms based on RAPTOR research across packet arrival intervals
Queried real-time Tor metrics archive to cross-reference historical relay uptime and bandwidth capacities
Generated probabilistic confidence scores rather than deterministic claims to assist law enforcement forensic documentation
case_study.outcome: Successfully demonstrated entry-guard correlation on forensic lab test captures with high confidence scoring.

featured_projects.title: Enterprise Secure Company Network Architecture
featured_projects.description: Master-level multi-tier enterprise network architecture designed in Cisco Packet Tracer, featuring Cisco ASA firewalls with three security zones (Inside, Outside, DMZ), dual-ISP BGP/failover, HSRP redundancy, OSPF routing, and VLAN segmentation.
features: Cisco ASA Firewall architecture enforcing strict zone security policies across Outside (security 0), DMZ (security 50), and Inside (security 100)
Dual-ISP backbone configuration providing automatic WAN failover and load balancing for high business availability
HSRP (Hot Standby Router Protocol) active/standby default gateway redundancy across core layer-3 distribution switches
6 department VLANs distributed across a 3-floor building topology with inter-VLAN routing and dynamic ACL inspection
DMZ server farm hosting public DNS, web, and email services isolated from internal corporate workstations and databases

case_study.problem: Growing mid-size enterprise networks suffer from flat unsegmented subnets, single points of failure at the WAN edge, and lack of firewall perimeter isolation.
case_study.built: Engineered a complete enterprise topology with dual-firewall perimeter, HSRP core switching, OSPF backbone, and multi-zone access control.
decisions: Segmented infrastructure into Inside, DMZ, and Outside security zones with stateful packet inspection on Cisco ASA
Configured HSRP on core switches to ensure sub-second failover for all department subnets
Isolated public-facing services into a dedicated DMZ to prevent lateral movement into corporate databases
case_study.outcome: Simulated full campus failure scenarios with 0 packet loss during primary link drops and verified strict isolation against unauthorized lateral scans.

community_projects.title: Hermes Agent Expert Knowledge Skill
community_projects.description: Comprehensive reference knowledge skill and specialized subagent bundle for Hermes Agent (Nous Research), providing instant architecture blueprints, configuration mastery, CLI tools, messaging gateway integration, and VPS hardening playbooks.
features: 16 structured knowledge modules covering agent architecture, VPS deployment, model providers, CLI commands, and toolsets
Specialized agent personas: Hermes Expert, Mission Planner, Troubleshooter, Cost Optimizer, and Security Auditor
Interactive playbook for Telegram, Discord, and WhatsApp messaging gateway setup with webhook and socket management
Automated cron scheduling, agent memory persistence, and multi-agent delegation pattern blueprints
Security hardening guidelines including PID namespace isolation, directory ACLs, and tool permission boundaries

case_study.problem: Operating autonomous AI agent systems like Hermes Agent requires navigating complex tool configuration, VPS runtime environments, and messaging gateways without unified reference material.
case_study.built: Authored a modular knowledge skill system with 16 reference guides and 5 domain-specific agent definitions formatted for instant retrieval.
decisions: Structured reference chapters by operational domain (foundations, tools, messaging, security, memory)
Packaged specialized subagent system prompts optimized for specific tasks like debugging and cost auditing
Mapped agent tool integration against open Model Context Protocol (MCP) standards
case_study.outcome: Created the definitive technical knowledge base for Hermes Agent adopted by builders for autonomous server management.

community_projects.title: Hermes Agent Skill Forge & Playbooks
community_projects.description: Toolkit and playbook repository designed to build, test, and deploy production-grade agent skills, custom MCP server plugins, and autonomous workflows on the Hermes Agent platform.
features: Standardized skill scaffolding generator creating valid skill manifests, agent definitions, and reference directories
Pre-built playbooks for social media automation, content scheduling, continuous code review, and VPS monitoring
MCP server integration templates connecting Hermes agents to external APIs, databases, and filesystem tools
Automated skill verification linter checking YAML frontmatter, path resolution, and argument schemas
Multi-agent team orchestration scripts enabling supervisor and worker agent task division

case_study.problem: Developers creating custom skills for AI agents lack structured boilerplate, leading to inconsistent tool schemas and broken agent execution loops.
case_study.built: Created an open-source skill forge repository providing scaffolding templates, verification linters, and reusable playbooks.
decisions: Enforced agentskills.io and MCP open standards across all tool and skill configurations
Built automated linting to catch missing reference files and invalid yaml definitions before deployment
Included real-world playbooks for social automation and server management as reference implementations
case_study.outcome: Streamlined new agent skill creation from hours to minutes with turnkey testing and validation scripts.

community_projects.title: Cybersecurity Research Blog & Digital Garden
community_projects.description: Personal cybersecurity blog and technical portfolio built with modern static architecture, featuring deep-dive articles on ethical hacking, packet tracer architectures, AI agents, SOC automation, and real-world security experiments.
features: Clean, performance-optimized reader experience with dark cyber aesthetic, syntax highlighting, and responsive layout
Categorized technical publications spanning Networking, Enterprise Network Design, Tor, Social Engineering, and Mentorship
Interactive client-side search engine indexing article titles, tags, categories, and content for instant discovery
Automated GitHub Actions deployment pipeline building static assets and publishing directly to GitHub Pages
Structured open-graph metadata, RSS feeds, and semantic HTML maximizing search accessibility and syndication

case_study.problem: Documenting intricate cybersecurity experiments, packet tracer setups, and reverse-engineering findings requires a persistent, clean platform free of platform lock-in.
case_study.built: Developed a custom-themed static blog on Hexo hosted on GitHub Pages with automated CI/CD publishing.
decisions: Employed lightweight client-side search for rapid zero-latency article filtering without backend infrastructure
Designed clean cybersecurity-themed typographic hierarchy emphasizing code blocks and architecture diagrams
Configured automatic build-and-deploy pipelines via GitHub Actions on every markdown commit
case_study.outcome: Published comprehensive guides reaching hundreds of student peers and cybersecurity learners globally.

other_projects.title: Serverless Data Lake Architecture on AWS
other_projects.description: Scalable enterprise data lake architecture leveraging shared AWS Lambda layers, AWS Glue ETL jobs, Amazon EventBridge orchestration, Amazon S3 tiered storage, and automated data quality validation with quarantine handling.
features: Event-driven ingestion pipeline: file arrivals in raw S3 buckets trigger validation Lambda functions via EventBridge
Shared Lambda Layers centralizing common data transformation utilities, schema validation models, and third-party libraries
AWS Glue crawler and ETL jobs converting unstructured/JSON logs into partitioned Parquet format for fast Athena querying
Quarantine pattern: malformed records automatically isolated into dead-letter S3 buckets with CloudWatch alert notifications
Lifecycle tiering policies automatically transitioning raw data from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier for significant cost savings

case_study.problem: Disparate data silos and duplicated transformation logic across multiple services lead to bloated Lambda functions and slow analytics queries.
case_study.built: Engineered a serverless data lake pipeline using Lambda layers for code reuse and Glue ETL for columnar Parquet conversion.
decisions: Packaged data validation logic into shared Lambda Layers to prevent code drift across microservices
Converted raw records into columnar Snappy-compressed Parquet, reducing Athena query scan costs by ~80%
Configured automated dead-letter quarantine buckets to preserve erroneous payloads for developer inspection
case_study.outcome: Reduced data processing overhead by 70% and enabled ad-hoc SQL querying over millions of records with sub-second latency.

other_projects.title: Oracle to PostgreSQL Heterogeneous Migration
other_projects.description: Production-grade database migration blueprint moving enterprise workloads from on-premises Oracle databases to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL using AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) and Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) with continuous replication (CDC).
features: Automated schema conversion using AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) with automated data type and constraint translation
Full-load data migration combined with continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) replicating live transactions during transition
AWS DMS replication instances with multi-AZ high availability and optimized memory buffers for high transaction throughput
Comprehensive data validation task comparing source and target row counts, checksums, and table structures in real-time
Cutover plan minimizing business downtime to under 15 minutes by synchronizing transaction logs before final DNS switch

case_study.problem: Enterprise Oracle databases impose steep licensing fees and vendor lock-in, but live migration to open-source Aurora PostgreSQL risks downtime and data corruption.
case_study.built: Architected an end-to-end migration pipeline using AWS SCT for schema transformation and AWS DMS for zero-loss CDC replication.
decisions: Used AWS SCT to automatically convert ~85% of complex PL/SQL procedures and tables to PL/pgSQL
Implemented ongoing CDC replication alongside initial full load to allow parallel testing without stopping production
Configured automated CloudWatch alarms on DMS replication latency and memory utilization
case_study.outcome: Eliminated Oracle licensing overhead while achieving zero data loss and under 15 minutes total cutover downtime.
